headline_marked: Sangu and Matamuhuri rivers [[breach danger marks as floods swamp Bandarban]]
headline: Sangu and Matamuhuri rivers breach danger marks as floods swamp Bandarban
summary: Heavy rainfall and hill runoff have inundated low-lying areas, submerging homes and roads while disrupting communication with several upazilas.
details: Continuous heavy rainfall over the past four days and hill runoff have pushed water levels in the Sangu and Matamuhuri rivers above danger marks, flooding low-lying areas across Bandarban.
According to the BWDB, the Sangu river was flowing at 15.76 metres, exceeding its 14.80m danger level, while the Matamuhuri river stood at 11.93 metres against a danger level of 11.80 metres.

Floodwaters have submerged homes, roads, and cropland in Bandarban municipality and several upazilas, leaving many families marooned in their homes and disrupting road communication to Thanchi, Ruma, and Rowangchhari.
The district administration has prepared 220 emergency shelters, with around 700 people from 190 families having taken shelter by 11:00am today.
Authorities have warned of an increased risk of landslides due to prolonged rainfall, using loudspeakers to urge residents in vulnerable areas to move to safer locations.
Bandarban Deputy Commissioner Saniul Ferdous stated that UNOs, executive magistrates, and fire service personnel are on standby to handle possible flooding and landslides.
Despite the official reports, Bandarban Hill District Council Chairman Thanjama Lusai claimed there was no possibility of flooding in the district, citing a council member.
caption:

The district administration has prepared 220 emergency shelters, with around 700 people from 190 families having taken shelter by 11:00am today.
